clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; he and Celeste separated in August; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton and her mother by September; your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979 and her functioning came back. The shifts pile up across the extended family, each one's trouble near another's.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest ordered in March 1984, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house and overfunctioned; your father and Hazel argued over how the house was kept; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. Your sister Ines was born in September and the period settled. Three shifts beside the opening show the family's reactions in those months, and no one else's shifts show then.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within a decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father nightly for news of her; he and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather had chest pains by December 1990; by February 1996 he gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; your father drank most evenings by 1993 and fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. The trouble builds slowly across the years with no relief between steps, each person's move tied to Hazel's decline and the weight on those closest to her.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for the mines in May 1999, within months: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans to go north; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines everywhere, even to work. By August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts pass from one person to the next in those months, each one's trouble near another's.
